title: Airtel's revenue rises 16.7% to Rs 60,878 crore as earnings per user climb to Rs 271
dek: India's second-largest telecom operator added a record 12 lakh postpaid customers and cut its net debt by 14% in the September quarter. Reports differ on which profit figure to use.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bharti Airtel's consolidated revenue rose 16.7% from a year earlier to Rs 60,877.5 crore in the July-September quarter, the company told the stock exchanges on Thursday, as average revenue per user (ARPU) climbed to Rs 271 from Rs 256 a year ago. The company said higher earnings per customer, after changes to its mobile tariffs, drove the growth.

Revenue from India grew 9.4% to Rs 42,308 crore, reports said. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) were Rs 34,946 crore, up 5% from the previous quarter, with a margin of 57.4%, according to reports.

## Two profit figures

Reports of the quarter's profit differ. One report said that consolidated profit rose 24% to Rs 10,710 crore from Rs 8,651 crore a year earlier. Another reported consolidated net profit of Rs 8,887.5 crore, up 9% from Rs 8,167 crore in the April-June quarter. Companies with listed subsidiaries report profit both before and after deducting the share that belongs to minority shareholders in those subsidiaries, and the two reports appear to use different measures. The Declaration could not access the filing to confirm which is which.

## Customers and data use

ARPU is the telecom industry's main measure of pricing power. India mobile service revenue grew 10.1% from a year earlier, the company said, citing "strong customer additions and improved realisation".

Airtel's customer base across all its markets grew 11% to 69.25 crore. In India it has 49.86 crore customers, of whom 37.72 crore are mobile users. Home services, which include fixed-line broadband, grew about 29% to 1.53 crore customers.

The company added a record 12 lakh postpaid customers in the quarter, taking that base to 3.12 crore, and 29 lakh smartphone data customers. Average data use per customer rose 28.8% from a year earlier to 36.5 GB a month.

"India mobile delivered revenue growth of 3.4% QoQ, backed by our strategy of portfolio premiumisation and winning quality customers," executive vice-chairman Gopal Vittal said. He said the Africa business had a "standout quarter", with revenue up 6.7% from the previous quarter in constant currency.

## Spending and debt

Airtel spent Rs 12,467 crore on its networks and other capital projects in the quarter, Rs 9,908 crore of it in India. It added 497 towers and 11,684 mobile broadband base stations during the quarter, and 5,649 towers and 44,718 km of optical fibre over the past year. It also invested Rs 2,826 crore in a land parcel for data-centre expansion in India.

Net debt fell about 14% from a year earlier to Rs 1.66 lakh crore, from Rs 1.94 lakh crore.

## The competition

The results come weeks after Reliance's Jio Platforms listed on the stock exchanges in what one report called India's biggest-ever IPO. Jio leads the market by number of subscribers and by market value but earns less per user than Airtel, and reports have said that an industry-wide tariff increase is expected by the end of the 2026-27 financial year. Airtel's shares closed 0.52% lower at Rs 2,056.90 on the NSE on Thursday; the results came after market hours, reports said.
